### Issue URL (Anti Adblock Script) [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/faa-ground-stop-canceled-flights-travelers-what-we-know/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.cbsnews.com%2Fnews%2Ffaa-ground-stop-canceled-flights-travelers-what-we-know%2F) ### Comment > ### Issue Description > Anti-adblock wall on `cbsnews.com` via Admiral First-Party Proxy. > > * **A/B Test Behavior:** Clean/Incognito sessions are served an inescapable hard wall with no dismiss link and page scrolling locked (`overflow: hidden`). Some regular sessions occasionally receive a variant with a delayed *"I'll fix it next time"* dismiss button. > * **Consent Requirement:** Only triggers after OneTrust (`cbsoptanon`) allows targeting/advertising cookies (`cmp.ot.targetingAllowed`). > > ### Proxied Admiral Script URLs Observed > * `https://silkyslumber.com/static/kmxtcpfvq/q1zxupa.js` > * `https://topicspin.com/static/k6vi91qgp/siqqoqasp4mu874ckh6569s5n2uum.js` > > ### Inline Bootstrap & Obfuscation Details > * Admiral's inline loader is wrapped in `loadAdmiralScript()` and invoked asynchronously inside `cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady` $\rightarrow$ `cmp.ot.targetingAllowed`. > * Because `loadAdmiralScript()` runs asynchronously after `document.currentScript` is `null`, inline scriptlets hooking `document.createElement` do not catch it. > * Evades generic Admiral signatures by aliasing `decodeURI` (`D(D(Y))`) and double-encoding `'admiral'` (`%25%36%31%64m%25%36%39%25%37%32%2561%6C`). > * Static Admiral Property ID in inline script: `QS01RDlDQzI1QTgyQ0FFMzUwNTQ5RkMwQUMtMg` > > ### Suggested / Verified Fix > Aborting synchronously when `loadAdmiralScript` is registered with `cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady` blocks Admiral before any proxied scripts are fetched: > ```adblock > cbsnews.com#%#//scriptlet('abort-current-inline-script', 'cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady', 'loadAdmiralScript') > ``` ``` Username: @SpoiledSneeze ``` ### Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On www⁠.iafcertsearch.org a first-party cookie-consent sheet plus its fixed dimming backdrop cover the lower viewport and grey out the whole home page on load, matching the reporter's screenshot. The domain-scoped element-hiding rule iafcertsearch.org#⁠#⁠[⁠class*="cookie-consent-banner"]⁠ removed the sheet and backdrop and left the page intact and fully usable in the locked AdGuard CLI filtering session. ## Rule `iafcertsearch.org##[class*="cookie-consent-banner"]` ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie-consent notice (page-owned annoyance), not first-party advertising, not a paywall, not a German anti-adblock wall and not a scam/phishing page, so none of the instruction's closing rules applies. No maintainer rule blocks a cosmetic hide here:⁠ the consent sheet is hidden and the page afterwards works (content legible, no scroll lock, no popup return). No existing shared rule family covers this consent UI, so a new domain-scoped rule in the Cookie Notices filter is the appropriate fix. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/4812eff50c6ddf22a0a93b19014ac9d732ed18ca/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/44863997064 Automated analysis against filters at `4812eff`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

### Issue URL (Anti Adblock Script) [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/faa-ground-stop-canceled-flights-travelers-what-we-know/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.cbsnews.com%2Fnews%2Ffaa-ground-stop-canceled-flights-travelers-what-we-know%2F) ### Comment > ### Issue Description > Anti-adblock wall on `cbsnews.com` via Admiral First-Party Proxy. > > * **A/B Test Behavior:** Clean/Incognito sessions are served an inescapable hard wall with no dismiss link and page scrolling locked (`overflow: hidden`). Some regular sessions occasionally receive a variant with a delayed *"I'll fix it next time"* dismiss button. > * **Consent Requirement:** Only triggers after OneTrust (`cbsoptanon`) allows targeting/advertising cookies (`cmp.ot.targetingAllowed`). > > ### Proxied Admiral Script URLs Observed > * `https://silkyslumber.com/static/kmxtcpfvq/q1zxupa.js` > * `https://topicspin.com/static/k6vi91qgp/siqqoqasp4mu874ckh6569s5n2uum.js` > > ### Inline Bootstrap & Obfuscation Details > * Admiral's inline loader is wrapped in `loadAdmiralScript()` and invoked asynchronously inside `cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady` $\rightarrow$ `cmp.ot.targetingAllowed`. > * Because `loadAdmiralScript()` runs asynchronously after `document.currentScript` is `null`, inline scriptlets hooking `document.createElement` do not catch it. > * Evades generic Admiral signatures by aliasing `decodeURI` (`D(D(Y))`) and double-encoding `'admiral'` (`%25%36%31%64m%25%36%39%25%37%32%2561%6C`). > * Static Admiral Property ID in inline script: `QS01RDlDQzI1QTgyQ0FFMzUwNTQ5RkMwQUMtMg` > > ### Suggested / Verified Fix > Aborting synchronously when `loadAdmiralScript` is registered with `cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady` blocks Admiral before any proxied scripts are fetched: > ```adblock > cbsnews.com#%#//scriptlet('abort-current-inline-script', 'cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady', 'loadAdmiralScript') > ``` ``` Username: @SpoiledSneeze ``` ### Screenshots

issue.title: Remove AI filters from the Other Annoyances
issue.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I checked the documentation and found no answer;
- [x] I checked to make sure that this issue has not already been filed;
- [x] This is not an ad/bug report.

### Problem description

AdGuard Other Annoyances filter blocks AI features such as Google Search Overview.

### Proposed solution

Since AdGuard already offers an AI-annoyance blocking filter list (Stevo's AI Blocklist) I think that rules blocking AI should be removed from the Other Annoyances filter list. Additionally, while the filter provides many useful rules that block unnecessary clutter and other features, some users use these AI features and don't want them blocked, but still want the blocking power of the rest of the filter list. All in all, I think this should be done because there is already a specialized list for this specific purpose that is more comprehensive, and some users want to enable Other Annoyances without blocking AI features.

### Additional information

_No response_

comment.body: Surely the ideal win-win solution would be to spin off the Aİ entries into a new sub-list of AdGuard Annoyances. Something like "AdGuard Annoyances - Against AI Features" (I couldn't come up with a better example name in a hurry), so that they at least wouldn't be in "AdGuard Annoyances - Other Annoyances" anymore.

The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

www⁠.echo24.de is a German news site whose article page shows a German anti-adblock wall ("Bitte erlauben Sie Werbung auf dieser Website" with a "Werbung erlauben und fortfahren" button and an "Ich verwende keinen Adblocker" row), detected through html-load.com/ad-shield session scripts. This run's stated filter policy says German anti-adblock walls get no rule, so the report is recommended for closing rather than patched.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction, Filter policy:⁠ 'German anti-adblock walls:⁠ no rule; recommend closing. This covers only a German site's wall or popup that detects the ad blocker and asks to disable it or to allowlist the site.' The page itself shows exactly that wall:⁠ on www⁠.echo24.de (html lang="de", German regional news portal) a full-page German notice headed 'Bitte erlauben Sie Werbung auf dieser Website' with the primary button 'Werbung erlauben und fortfahren', a 'Brauchen Sie Hilfe?' mail link and the rows 'Ich verwende keinen Adblocker' and 'So erlauben Sie Werbung in Schul- und Unternehmensnetzwerken' — i.e. it detects the ad blocker and asks the visitor to allowlist the site. The instruction also requires checking what the page shows rather than the reporter's chosen problem type; the reporter's label 'T:⁠ Annoyance' does not change the classification. Per the same instruction the agent never closes an issue:⁠ this is a recommendation for a maintainer to check and decide.

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"48ff742a9af66e6e83fa167659c8a71c57b17abcd9104c37572d4c0cbf1d6361"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The Verge's "Please allow ads on this site" wall is built by an inline Ad-Shield detector that injects a full-viewport iframe from report.error-report.com, but the wall never appeared in the locked AdGuard CLI environment (desktop and mobile viewports, consent untouched and accepted; full-page vision:⁠ absent, no obstruction), so the wall-hiding candidate theverge.com#⁠#⁠iframe[⁠src^="https:⁠//report.error-report.com/modal"]⁠ could not be validated and is handed over for review.

## Candidate for review

`theverge.com##iframe[src^="https://report.error-report.com/modal"]`

BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt

Not verified: apply_rule could not judge it:⁠ on the filtered baseline no element matched the selector (inconclusive, baseline_symptom_absent), because the reported wall never fired here. Three sessions (desktop and mobile viewports, consent untouched and accepted) loaded theverge.com with status 200 and full-page vision called the interstitial absent with no obstruction; the page's own inline Ad-Shield detector ran and cached cache_is_blocking_ads=true and its html-load.com SDK loaded, yet error-report.com was never requested and no overlay iframe appeared. The reporter's iOS/Safari advanced-protection setup and its skipped third-party lists cannot be exercised here, so absence is an environment limit, not proof the wall is gone. The rule hides the fixed 100vw/100vh modal iframe the detector appends; never visually verified.

comment.body:
<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"7e645d692a3630b8967711a9455937322cf37decfeffb716ffd1a99135bfb92d"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The MangaWorld homepage loads two live popunder ad networks (pubadx with an armed pxpop probe, and an iclick-style tag via naupsithizeekee.com/luugy.com) that match the reporter's click-hijack complaint, but no click in the unfiltered or reporter-profile sessions opened a tab or redirected, and the full-page capture of the filtered page shows no popup or ad element. The run carries the `prevent-window-open` scriptlet for mangaworld.* for human review; the reporter's own filter set already blocks all four ad tags behind the behaviour.

## Candidate for review

`mangaworld.*#%#//scriptlet('prevent-window-open')`

ItalianFilter/sections/specific.txt

Not verified: apply_rule ran the candidate in the reporter-profile session and the visual review returned 'inconclusive' with symptom 'unclear':⁠ a tab or window opened by a click cannot be seen in static captures. The rehearsed click sequence (click #⁠hero-stage, wait, click main, wait) opened 0 popups in every phase - unfiltered A, baseline B and candidate C - with identical revealSteps results, so neither the presence of the click-hijack nor its resolution could be demonstrated. pageIntegrity stayed intact with the candidate; remainingInstances, observedDamage and adLayoutResidue were empty. The same clicks in the unfiltered control session also opened no tab and caused no redirect, so the behavioural symptom never appeared in this environment and the candidate stays browser-unverified.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/44886665562

<sub>Automated analysis against filters at `3e12a93`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.</sub>

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reporter's annotation targets the fixed green WhatsApp chat button that stays pinned over the datacenter cards on dcloud.co.id/speed-test.html. A domain-scoped element-hiding rule in the AdGuard Widgets filter, `dcloud.co.id##a.fixed[href^="https://api.whatsapp.com/send"]`, hides that floating widget while leaving the site's inline WhatsApp contact link visible, and it passed verified before/after validation with no page damage or residue. ## Rule `dcloud.co.id##a.fixed[href^="https://api.whatsapp.com/send"]` ## Policy rationale Run instruction filter policy:⁠ the report is neither the site's own advertising, nor a paywall, nor a German anti-adblock wall, nor another anti-adblock wall — it is an annoyance (a floating third-party-style chat widget), so no policy rule closes it. Filter policy (AdGuard Widgets filter):⁠ chat widgets that are not integrated with the content and are not the main content of the page are blocked by the Widgets filter; this WhatsApp floating chat button is exactly that kind of widget. Maintainer rules:⁠ no existing shared rule fits without damage (the only similar multi-domain rule hides every api.whatsapp.com/send anchor, which would also hide this site's inline WhatsApp contact link in the page content), so a new domain-scoped rule is the correct form. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Widgets/sections/widgets.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/5012f7dc9ac335e076956eb81966bd3679d943e7/AnnoyancesFilter/Widgets/sections/widgets.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"1b55b580c585773bbc12e768d55416268ba514ada1288bae1106e19b3406a93d"} -->
The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

The blank band the reporter annotated is the site's own fixed-height reservation for its scoreboard/promotion unit:⁠ the wrapper keeps min-height 341px (450px on mobile) while the rendered matchup card is 166px, its first-party promotions feed returned 204 No Content, and no filter or blocked request acts on the region. Per the run instruction's policy this is the site's own (first-party) advertising space, so no rule is proposed and the report is recommended for closing.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction filter policy:⁠ "The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing." The annotated blank band is the site's own reserved promotion/advertising space:⁠ the story page's first-party promotions feed for the placement above the story header (`/api/v2/promotions/story-template-legacy-2-above-header/26`) answered 204 No Content, and the space around the scoreboard card is kept at a fixed height by the site's own stylesheet. Nothing in the band was filtered or blocked:⁠ `get_applied_rules` (AdGuard CLI) reports no element-hiding rule acting on it, no ad element/iframe exists inside it (the page's `.s-advert` slots are all outside it and 0-height), and no blocked request would have filled it. Removing the whitespace would require overriding the site's own layout/promotion reservation (a `#$#` min-height override), which is a deliberate change to the site's own advertising space, not a filtering fix. The block of the site's ad framework `||htlbid.com^` (AdGuard Base) is a general filtering rule; per policy the site's own advertising "should not be unblocked if the blocking is caused by general filtering rules", so no unblocking rule is warranted either. A maintainer should still confirm:⁠ this environment offers no unfiltered control (the proxy filters every session), and the reporter's iOS mobile layout could not be re-rendered (two mobile navigation timeouts), so the attribution to the site's own promotion unit rests on marking up and geometry evidence rather than on an unfiltered A/B capture.

The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

With the reporter's exact settings the reported page shows only its own "Loading..." splash:⁠ its two third-party ad-network loaders are already blocked by an existing general Base-filter rule for random-letter *.in ad scripts, and unfiltered the page navigates away by itself, so there is no ad, popup or overlay left for a rule to remove. No rule can fix this — restoring the page would mean unblocking general-rule blocking, which filter policy forbids — so the report should be closed for a maintainer to check.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Policy rationale

Run instruction:⁠ "The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing." The page is nothing but the site's own ad-delivery/redirect gateway:⁠ its first-party inline framework (RZId/RVId config, Base "https:⁠//ablelaunchshorts.com/rdl/e/mitb/2060440") and a hidden click anchor a.c[⁠href="/r/bl/2060440"]⁠, with no other content on the page. Filter policy (linked by the run instruction), Ad blocking filters § Limitations and exceptions:⁠ "The site’s own advertising should not be deliberately blocked. However, it should not be unblocked if the blocking is caused by general filtering rules." The only change that would make the reported page render is unblocking zafossbwimwu.in/ognxco and atdzfavz.in/ognxco, which the general Base-filter rule for random-letter *.in ad scripts blocks — so an exception is ruled out and no genuine ad element is left to hide. Hiding the page's splash (#⁠loader) would leave an empty page and fix nothing, and blocking the whole site on obfuscation and bot-fingerprinting indicators alone would be an unsupported high-risk action for a maintainer, not an agent decision. There is therefore no B/C capture, no vision verdict and no page-integrity check for this candidate. It rests on live read-only evidence only:⁠ the mobile page computes `#main-content { margin-top: 282px }` from the site's rule `...global-top-ad-enabled:not(:has(.s-advert .htl-ad)) + .sidearm-app-content-container #main-content { margin-top: calc(var(--main-nav-height) + var(--sport-nav-height) + 122px) }`, matching because `||htlbid.com^` blocks htlbid.js so no `.htl-ad` renders, while the site's own `width <= 768px` media query sets that margin to 0. Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — goairforcefalcons.com leaves an empty 82px fixed white band with a grey "Close Ad" X at the top of mobile pages once its third-party top-ad creative (htlbid/adsbygoogle) is blocked - the blank strip the reporter annotated. The verified rule removes div#⁠global-top-ad, which also drops the inline :⁠root height variable reserving that space, so the band and its 82px gap disappear with no residue or page damage. ## Rule `goairforcefalcons.com#?#div#global-top-ad:remove()` ## Policy rationale No run-instruction rule closes this report:⁠ the top band is not the site's own (first-party) advertising, not a paywall and not an anti-adblock wall. The band is the site's third-party programmatic top ad slot - its creative loaders htlbid.com (header bidding) and pagead2.googlesyndication.com are third-party ad platforms already blocked by the AdGuard Base filter - so a filter rule for the leftover is in scope. Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — omahamavs.com (a Sidearm Sports site) keeps an empty 82px white "global top ad" bar pinned across the top of its mobile pages with only a "Close Ad" X, because its ad loader htlbid.com is already blocked by the Base filter. The domain-scoped element hiding rule omahamavs.com#⁠#⁠#⁠global-top-ad was verified:⁠ the bar and its reserved 82px are gone and the page stays intact, and it extends the identical existing rule for gophersports.com. ## Rule `omahamavs.com###global-top-ad` ## Policy rationale Not the site's own advertising:⁠ the bar's slot is filled by the third-party ad framework htlbid.com, whose loader is already blocked by the general Base-filter rule `||htlbid.com^`; what remains is an empty leftover ad container with its own 'Close Ad' control, and the fix hides only that leftover without unblocking any ad. Not a paywall, and not an anti-adblock wall:⁠ no detector script, overlay request or gate appears in the captured 219-request HAR or the DOM, so the German anti-adblock clause and the other-anti-adblock clause of the run instruction do not apply. A standard domain-scoped element hiding `##` rule was tried first and verified; no CSS injection, ExtendedCSS, scriptlet or network rule was needed. ## Place in the list [BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/5012f7dc9ac335e076956eb81966bd3679d943e7/BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — miamiredhawks.com leaves an empty 66px black top-ad bar (`#global-top-ad`, only a "Close Ad" X) pinned over the mobile page once the Base filter's `||htlbid.com^` blocks the ad, matching the reporter's screenshot. The domain-scoped rule `miamiredhawks.com###global-top-ad` was verified with apply_rule:⁠ symptom resolved, page integrity intact, no remaining instances. ## Rule `miamiredhawks.com###global-top-ad` ## Policy rationale Not the site's own (first-party) advertising:⁠ the container is a Sidearm top ad slot served by the third-party htlbid ad server and is empty after `||htlbid.com^` blocked it, so the policy's 'own advertising' exception does not apply. Not a paywall and not an anti-adblock wall:⁠ the article is fully readable, no detector request appears in the captured traffic and the page shows no gate or popup asking to disable the blocker. The symptom is a leftover empty ad container, which this repository handles with a domain-scoped element-hiding rule (existing precedent for the same platform:⁠ `gophersports.com###global-top-ad`). ## Place in the list [BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/5012f7dc9ac335e076956eb81966bd3679d943e7/BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reporter's ad redirect when changing manga chapters could not be reproduced:⁠ every manga chapter reader page is served a server-rendered "Ce chapitre n'est pas disponible (503)" overlay and fires no ad request, and all reachable pages show no popup on any chapter-change click. The only ad infrastructure seen is already handled by the baseline, so the run carries one narrow unverified candidate — a prevent-window-open scriptlet for scan-manga.com — for human review.

## Candidate for review

`scan-manga.com#%#//scriptlet('prevent-window-open')`

BaseFilter/sections/general_extensions.txt

Not verified: The reported ad redirect could not be produced in any phase. Every manga chapter reader page on the site is served a server-rendered 'Ce chapitre n'est pas disponible (503)' overlay as the first body child and fires no ad request, and the reachable pages (home, series page, working novel reader) opened no tab and made no ad-host request across three click rehearsals. The single apply_rule experiment returned environmentExperiment 'inconclusive' with validationSkipped and errorKind baseline_symptom_absent (its chapter-link revealStep did not complete in the first phase, and that session then lost its filtering proxy), so no visual review judged the candidate; the replacement session's profile differed, so the locked validation baseline could not be reused for a further experiment. The candidate is also not replaceable by a vendor network rule:⁠ the reader's only ad reference, pemsrv.com, is already blocked globally by ||s.pemsrv.com^$all and ||a.pemsrv.com/popunder*.js.

## Missing information

- No run-instruction guidance for an unreachable ad-redirect flow whose ad stack is on a server-gated page: The issue reports behavioural ad redirects that appear while changing manga chapters. In the locked environment every manga chapter reader page (/lecture-en-ligne/...) is served a server-rendered "Ce chapitre n'est pas disponible (503)" overlay as its first body child and fires no ad request, so the flow that carries the ad stack cannot be exercised; only reachable pages (home, series page, novel reader) could be rehearsed and they show no redirect. The run instruction says how to treat a proven click-opened ad tab (scriptlet + revealSteps rehearsal) and how to treat a loadable vendor script seen in the network log, but not what evidence suffices, or which candidate is preferred, when neither a rehearsal nor a captured ad request is obtainable within the locked environment.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reporter's marked red blocks on unionathletics.com are empty Google Ad Manager slots:⁠ the site paints .sidearm-dfp-ad bright red, and because the ad scripts are blocked the 300x250 and 320x50 slots never fill. Hiding the ad containers with a domain-scoped rule was verified in the browser:⁠ both red placeholders disappear, page height drops by exactly their 396px, and all page content stays intact. ## Rule `unionathletics.com##.dfp, .sidearm-dfp-ad` ## Policy rationale Not the site's own advertising:⁠ the leftover placeholders are third-party Google Ad Manager (DFP) slots served via securepubads.g.doubleclick.net with header bidding, not first-party ads; the site's own sponsor carousels are untouched by the rule. Not a paywall and not an anti-adblock wall:⁠ no detector script or message appears; the annoyance is empty ad-slot placeholders left by already-blocked ad requests. The reporter typed it as Annoyance and the leftovers are exactly that kind of ad-residue annoyance, which this repository handles with element-hiding rules. ## Place in the list [BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/5012f7dc9ac335e076956eb81966bd3679d943e7/BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — 225225.jp leaves three 336x280 Google Ad Manager slots unrendered, so the page keeps \~846px of blank dark space — the reporter's empty panels — and the repository already has the matching shared rule `adr-stock.com,nikkei225jp.com##.winAD` in the Japanese filter. The candidate `225225.jp,adr-stock.com,nikkei225jp.com##.winAD` collapsed every ad wrapper to zero height with the page intact, but the vision review kept flagging ordinary dark-page gaps as ad residue, so the rule is carried unverified for human review.

## Candidate for review

`225225.jp,adr-stock.com,nikkei225jp.com##.winAD`

JapaneseFilter/sections/specific.txt

Not verified: apply_rule ran the candidate twice and environmentExperiment stayed inconclusive while visualReview rejected it with adLayoutResidue present, symptom not_resolved and two 'remaining' dark bands (after-capture y≈1956-2768 and y≈5216-6028); pageIntegrity was intact and observedDamage empty, and no ad returned. The DOM checks the review judged show all 8 .winAD wrappers collapsing from 280px to 0, #⁠adsMid/#⁠adsBtm from 282px to 0, all 8 Google Ad Manager slot divs inside .winAD, and the document shrinking 7596px to 6750px. Re-inspecting the two named AFTER tiles with the vision model found ordinary rankings/calendar content and plain inter-section spacing on the page's dark background, i.e. no ad element left:⁠ the residual bands are the dark page's own layout rather than the ad footprint, so no distinct rule can clear them without damaging layout.

## Still visible after the rule

- Document y=1956..2768 — dark empty band between the chart-control pill row (leftmost dark circle with "?") and the 「値上がり指数上位」 heading with the blue X icon — Full-width empty dark panel occupying the gap below the chart controls and above the 「値上がり指数上位」 rankings list. It shows no ad creative, no 336x280 frame, no REKLAMA-style label and no placeholder text — only reserved blank dark space where the ad slot sits unrendered. The same band is visible in the overlapping tiles 0f5c0825-4775-4d2f-b092-9219be1d61ea and d7cb8e2b-7b0e-4ed1-b7fe-f559f7f0f6cf at the same vertical position.
- Between the 11月東京都区部消費者物価指数 calendar rows and the 'プラスマネスの色を変更' site-settings panel — Large reserved dark blank area with no ad creative, ad label, frame, or placeholder block visible; leftover empty advertising height where an ad slot sits but no ad renders.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On gamertweak.com's article page the reporter's large blank band under the header is a leftover empty AdSense wrapper:⁠ `body > div.ad-fixed-container` keeps a 250px inline height while its `ins.adsbygoogle` is hidden and adsbygoogle.js is redirected. Adding `gamertweak.com##.ad-fixed-container` removed that band in the verified before/after experiment with page integrity intact and no damage. ## Rule `gamertweak.com##.ad-fixed-container` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale Run instruction policy:⁠ the rule is neither first-party advertising nor a paywall, and it is not a German anti-adblock wall; none of the close/no-rule rules applies. The target is a third-party AdSense slot whose wrapper keeps reserved height after filtering, i.e. leftover empty space on a site with sufficient traffic; the repository keeps this site's ad rules in BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt. No existing shared rule covers `.ad-fixed-container` (selector search returned no match), so a new domain-scoped element-hiding rule is the appropriate fix rather than an extension of a shared family. ## Place in the list [BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/5012f7dc9ac335e076956eb81966bd3679d943e7/BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt) Next to the site's existing rules, before [line 8387](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/5012f7dc9ac335e076956eb81966bd3679d943e7/BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt#L8387). ## Screenshots

The empty gray strip in the same screenshot is the leftover of the site's own Instant Gaming ad spot already hidden by a generic Base filter rule; both leftover candidates cleared it per the DOM probe but were refused by the vision review, so it is left for the maintainer. ## Rule `topgamesitalia.com##.sgcc-main-wrapper` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The verified defect is a cookie-consent notice from the site's consent plugin, which is the declared purpose of the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter — not first-party advertising, not a paywall, not an anti-adblock wall, so none of the instruction's recommend-close rules applies. The notice gates nothing:⁠ article content is fully visible and the page scrolls in both the filtered and unfiltered sessions, so hiding it cannot break a page function. The fix extends an existing shared multi-domain rule for this exact plugin instead of adding a per-site one-off, as the maintainer rules require. No rule is proposed for the empty gray strip under the navigation:⁠ that space belongs to the site's own advertising spot already hidden by a generic Base filter rule, and its leftover candidates could not be verified. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/2af5a252ae9e9b5c7b84533fa8f8470d6e179ce6/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 3989](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/2af5a252ae9e9b5c7b84533fa8f8470d6e179ce6/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L3989). ## Screenshots

### Comment
> False positive: opositors.cat is listed as Phishing since 2026-11-21 (see https://reports.adguard.com/en/opositors.cat/report.html).
> 
> opositors.cat is a public information portal about civil-service exams (oposicions) in Catalonia, Spain. It lists official job calls from public administrations with links to the official sources. It does not ask for passwords or payment data and does not imitate any other site. It is hosted on Vercel; Google Safe Browsing and Yandex Safe Browsing do not list it.
> 
> With AdGuard DNS (Default server, set as Private DNS on Android), Chrome shows ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR because the domain resolves to the AdGuard block page.
> 
> Steps to reproduce: use AdGuard DNS Default server, open https://opositors.cat/
>

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"c98fffbda2d9f069529dd23c224623099710324598e52f20a5226a851990df59"} -->
The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

On www⁠.naver.com the only difference between the reporter's filtered and unfiltered screenshots is Naver's own first-party premium ad slot (`#ad_premium_area`):⁠ its creatives are blocked by `||ssl.pstatic.net/melona/libs/` from the reporter's extra filterslist-KO Classic list, leaving broken alt text and a reserved 1920x760 band, while every content module, widget and the footer render intact and the repository's own Base+Mobile baseline shows no breakage at all. Because the damaged region is the site's own first-party advertising, the run instruction's policy ("no rule; recommend closing") forbids both unblocking it and hiding it, so no rule is proposed.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Policy rationale

Run instruction, Filter policy:⁠ "The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing." The whole damaged region on www⁠.naver.com is Naver's own first-party premium display slot, so both repair directions are excluded. AdGuard filter policy, Ad blocking filters ⁠> Limitations and exceptions:⁠ "The site's own advertising should not be deliberately blocked. However, it should not be unblocked if the blocking is caused by general filtering rules." An exception that lets the blocked creatives load unblocks the site's own advertising, and a cosmetic rule that removes the slot deliberately blocks advertising this repository's own baseline renders normally. The blocking behind the report comes from `||ssl.pstatic.net/melona/libs/` and `||sstatic.naver.net/melona/libs/` in the reporter's extra list (filterslist-KO Classic filter list, id 227), which this repository does not maintain; with the repository's official baseline (AdGuard Base + AdGuard Mobile Ads) the page shows no broken image and no residue, so there is no rule for this repository to write.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/44906069764

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — meiwakudenwa.jp reserves a 250px blank band for an unfilled AdSense slot in the article ad wrapper div.mwd-phone-ad-advice, producing the tall empty gap the reporter screenshotted. Adding meiwakudenwa.jp#⁠#⁠.mwd-phone-ad-advice to the Japanese filter collapses the gap; the bound experiment verified the symptom resolved with page integrity intact. ## Rule `meiwakudenwa.jp##.mwd-phone-ad-advice` ## Policy rationale None of the run instruction's closing rules applies:⁠ the element is a third-party AdSense ad slot, not the site's own first-party advertising, not a paywall, and not an anti-adblock wall. The defect is a leftover empty ad container that reserves layout space, which the repository fixes with an ordinary domain-scoped element-hiding rule. ## Place in the list [JapaneseFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/6d2e084f5137ffdbb8998b7205521258aa8bd829/JapaneseFilter/sections/specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — vide-greniers.org's own first-party detector (/v2/layout_head.js -⁠> AGW.hasBlocker(), which probes pagead2.googlesyndication.com/pagead/js/adsbygoogle.js) opens the served full-screen dialog 'Soutenez le réseau des agendas' with the reporter's "disable your ad blocker" text a few seconds after every load, covering the agenda and locking scroll. Hiding that dialog element with vide-greniers.org#⁠#⁠dialog[⁠x-ref="dialogAGW"]⁠ was validated (dialog visible in baseline, gone with the rule, page content readable and intact), so the rule is proposed for AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/antiadblock.txt. ## Rule `vide-greniers.org##dialog[x-ref="dialogAGW"]` ## Policy rationale The wall is a French-language page, so the instruction's German anti-adblock close-out does not apply. The captured requests show the detector:⁠ the first-party detector module /v2/layout_head.js (displayPaywall -⁠> AGW.hasBlocker) and its probe request to pagead2.googlesyndication.com/pagead/js/adsbygoogle.js, which the baseline blocks and which makes hasBlocker() return true. The wall is aggressive:⁠ it opens full-screen over the agenda content on every page load and locks page scrolling, effectively preventing use of the site (filter policy:⁠ anti-adblock walls that effectively prevent using the website are blocked). ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/antiadblock.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/6d2e084f5137ffdbb8998b7205521258aa8bd829/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/antiadblock.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"bf686acc60bd987b13c88302819d78e97470d4df6311f0144d12a7f33dab78dc"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — Environment:⁠ the report comes from AdGuard for iOS v4.5.25, which filters at network level, so the environment was locked to adguard_cli; AdGuard CLI 1.4.13 was prepared and its proxy filtered the page. Execution provenance is the CLI proxy in Chromium; the reporter's iOS app, Safari content blocker and DNS never ran (mobile execution-model conflict recorded — the candidate is plain #⁠#⁠ element hiding, which Safari content blockers support). Evidence:⁠ the reported article loaded (HTTP 200) and get_network_log shows no ad host, only first-party assets plus social/GTM/weather hosts, so the advertising is baked into the served HTML and element hiding is the right instrument. Ad-slot inspection plus DOM measurement inventoried the compensated ad family:⁠ #⁠js-cta/.p-entry__cta, an in-article 350×250 banner linked to /syouheikou with the text beginning "PR：いわき市北部地域を中心に…" (社会福祉法人 昌平黌); and four sidebar image widgets in #⁠side_col — #⁠media_image-13 (alt "広告バナー(常光サービス)"), #⁠media_image-11, #⁠media_image-5 ("【いわき信用組合】広告"), #⁠media_image-2 — each linking to an advertiser site or an advertiser PR page hosted by the paper. Scrolling lazy-loaded the creatives and full-page tile vision confirmed them as advertisement banners. #⁠footer_banner's three items link only to the paper's own category pages and its advertising guide, i.e. self-promotion that the policy protects; the AdSense placeholder renders display:⁠none and its loader is never requested. Policy:⁠ these banners advertise third-party businesses for compensation, which the policy's self-promotion definition excludes, so they are blockable advertising rather than "the site's own advertising"; the report is not a paywall, not a German anti-adblock wall, and shows no anti-adblock wall or detector request, so nothing in the instruction closes it and rule generation is allowed. (shortened; the full text is in the run artifacts)

## Missing information

- issue screenshot #⁠247765 unreadable by vision (size cap) and blocks inspect_full_page_capture: analyze_screenshot(issueScreenshotIndex=1) fails twice with "Vision image exceeds the 5242880-byte cap (6322951 bytes)", and inspect_full_page_capture refuses with issue_screenshot_analysis_required until that screenshot is analyzed. So the reporter-defined annotated target cannot be read and the tiled full-page vision batch over the live page is blocked. Tile artifacts from the live page can still be analyzed individually via analyze_screenshot(artifactId), which is what I am using instead.
- Vision byte cap on issue screenshot #⁠247765 blocks apply_rule and finish_fix themselves: The host gates both apply_rule and finish_fix on a successful analyze_screenshot of issue screenshot index 1, but analyze_screenshot refuses that image on every call with "Vision image exceeds the 5242880-byte cap (6322951 bytes)" (5 attempts, also after re-fetching the issue). Consequences in this run:⁠ (1) the reporter's annotated target cannot be read, so the exact ad the reporter complained about is unknown; (2) inspect_full_page_capture is refused with issue_screenshot_analysis_required; (3) apply_rule is refused with issue_screenshot_analysis_required, so no candidate can be validated; (4) finish_fix is rejected with issue_screenshot_analysis_required even for an analysis_only outcome, which is the only honest outcome left. A downscaled variant of the issue screenshot, or a way for the vision tool to re-encode oversized report images, is missing from the run.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — vinteconto.com.br shows an aggressive anti-adblock modal (full-screen SweetAlert2, allowOutsideClick disabled, body scroll locked) driven by an inline page script that fires whenever the first-party cookie `adblockmessage` is absent. A domain-scoped set-cookie scriptlet `vinteconto.com.br#%#//scriptlet('set-cookie', 'adblockmessage', 'true')` was verified:⁠ the modal is present in the filtered baseline and gone with the candidate, page integrity intact. ## Rule `vinteconto.com.br#%#//scriptlet('set-cookie', 'adblockmessage', 'true')` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The wall is not a German anti-adblock wall:⁠ the page and modal are Brazilian/Portuguese (vinteconto.com.br), so the German-wall no-rule instruction does not apply. This is another anti-adblock wall, and the page evidence captured by the run shows the detector:⁠ the inline detector script is part of the captured document request https:⁠//vinteconto.com.br/ and its logic (`!document.getElementById('xKykEzWqCLjT') && !Cookies.get('adblockmessage')`) was read from the live DOM; the triggering blocked first-party ad script /js/oncc-ad.js is in the captured network log. The wall qualifies for blocking under the filter policy's anti-adblock criteria:⁠ allowOutsideClick is false, a full-viewport backdrop covers the content, and body scroll is locked (computed overflow hidden), so it effectively prevents using the website. The site's own advertising is already blocked only by general Base filter rules (/oncc-ad.js$script, ||pagead2.googlesyndication.com^); no exception is proposed for it and no first-party ad is targeted by the new rule. ## Place in the list [BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/13d3f8b3e52827249b72add20a138ecc7419fe11/BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/44914983569 Automated analysis against filters at `13d3f8b`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reported doumori.gamewith.jp URL 301-redirects to gamewith.jp, where the Razer Gold banner is a server-rendered in-article ad module (div.gamedb-steam-ad) that survives the Base + Japanese + Mobile Ads baseline. gamewith.jp#⁠#⁠.gamedb-steam-ad was verified by apply_rule (ad visible before, hidden after, no residue, no remaining instances, page intact), but the finish_fix scope contract requires the rule to be scoped to doumori.gamewith.jp alone, and that form cannot match the redirected gamewith.jp page, so the verified rule is handed to a human.

## Candidate for review

`gamewith.jp##.gamedb-steam-ad`

JapaneseFilter/sections/specific.txt

Not verified: This rule WAS verified by apply_rule (environmentExperiment "verified", visualReview "verified":⁠ symptom resolved, adLayoutResidue absent, remainingInstances empty, pageIntegrity intact, adElementStatus visible→hidden), but the finish_fix contract refuses it because it requires the candidate to have exactly one positive scope for the reported domain doumori.gamewith.jp. That form was tried and is inert here:⁠ the reported host answers 301 and the ad renders on https:⁠//gamewith.jp/gamedb/1197, so doumori.gamewith.jp#⁠#⁠.gamedb-steam-ad matched no document and the ad stayed visible; the dual-domain form also cannot be carried because its review named remaining instances. The human decision needed is the rule's scope:⁠ gamewith.jp (validated, covers doumori.gamewith.jp pages after the redirect) versus the reported host alone (validated as ineffective). It belongs beside gamewith.jp#⁠#⁠.gamedb-steam-ad-compact in the existing gamewith.jp group of the AdGuard Japanese filter.

## Still visible after the rule

- Right sidebar, inside the 最新ニュース card:⁠ between the 最新ニュース heading and the first news item (『推しバズ』限定PUガチャ…), at the same height as the 'どうぶつの森 ポケットキャンプの画像' heading in the main column — A plainly reserved but unfilled advertising region of roughly sidebar width by \~150 px (the classic 300x250-style sidebar slot height) sits directly under the 最新ニュース heading. It is completely blank:⁠ no creative, no AD/PR badge, no advertiser name, no artwork and no text; the surrounding card border and the news items below are ordinary page furniture rather than part of the slot. The empty area is far taller than the ordinary spacing used between other cards/sections on the same page, so it remains a reserved advertising footprint in the page layout. No Razer Gold creative or any other ad artwork appears in it.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — dengekionline.com article pages leave three large blank bands (below the byline, mid-article, and above 関連記事) because empty Google Ad Manager slot wrappers keep a reserved 180-280px height once gpt.js is blocked. One element-hiding rule on those wrappers removes the ad footprint (measured display:⁠none, 0px, gap 280-⁠>0) with page integrity intact, but the bound vision review kept calling the article's own YouTube video blocks residue, so the rule is handed to a human unverified rather than published.

## Candidate for review

`dengekionline.com##div:has(> div > div[id^="dol-s_"][id$="_gam"])`

JapaneseFilter/sections/specific.txt

Not verified: apply_rule ran the candidate twice (second run identical rule, with four rehearsed domChecks); environmentExperiment stayed inconclusive and visualReview rejected it only for ad layout residue:⁠ symptom not_resolved with two remaining blank bands. Both phases' domChecks show those bands are the page's own media, not ad residue:⁠ div.ptIMRW_videoContents blocks holding titled YouTube players (youtube.com/embed/mC7t9DIL8kw and /twVrqAeJH1E, 355x200, zero _gam slots) that render white in the headless capture. In the same run every Google Ad Manager wrapper ends display:⁠none at 0px (baseline:⁠ 180px and 280px reserved) and the 280px gap between the breadcrumb and the 関連記事 section closes to 0, with pageIntegrity intact and observedDamage empty.

## Still visible after the rule

- 11月5日より1周年記念イベントを開催予定 — Large empty white band (roughly 250–300 px tall on a 375 px wide viewport) between the paragraph ending 「…サービス開始1周年に向けた今後の展開への期待が高まる内容となっています。」 and the blue section heading 「11月5日より1周年記念イベントを開催予定」, where the in-article ad unit should appear. comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — nara-speller.co.kr/speller/ ends in empty Geniee ad-slot residue — a 91px empty light-grey reserved slot box above the footer plus a 250px blank interstitial strip below it that stretches the page past the viewport. The domain-scoped cosmetic rule hiding both empty slot containers was verified in the filtering proxy:⁠ all leftovers collapse, the page is intact, and no residue remains. ## Rule `nara-speller.co.kr##div[id*="_nara-speller.co.kr_"], div[class*="min-h-[6.5rem]"]` ## Policy rationale The leftover comes from third-party ad-network slots (Geniee:⁠ cpt.geniee.jp loader, aladdin.genieesspv.jp/ad_call, prebid bidders), not from the site's own first-party advertising, so the 'site's own advertising:⁠ no rule' rule does not apply. The page shows no paywall and no anti-adblock wall or detection message, so no rule of the instruction closes this report. The fix is a domain-scoped cosmetic element-hiding rule for empty ad containers, which is the repository's standard treatment for ad leftovers and does not block or unblock any network request. ## Place in the list [BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/18cba123dcb48b0a2b5dd5be7afb9308ab897ab9/BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Missing information - Rule-placement documents do not list the per-filter section files (e.g. Base filter sections), and AdguardFilters has no Korean language filter: The run instruction deliberately leaves placement to "files per language and per rule kind across <⁠Filter⁠>/sections/*.txt", and the served CONTRIBUTING "Rule placement" / "AdGuard Base filter" sections only point at the Base folder URL, not at the individual section files. The contributing guide's repository-structure headings list Russian, Ukrainian, Chinese, Dutch, French, German, Japanese, Spanish and Turkish language filters, but no Korean one, so a Korean-site rule has no declared language bucket. I resolved the file from search_rules evidence instead:⁠ BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt is reported by search_rules as holding site-specific element-hiding rules (e.g. leitesculinaria.com#⁠#⁠.ad-wrap, ah-me.com#⁠#⁠#⁠ad_banner). A listing of which section file each rule kind belongs in (site-specific element hiding vs foreign-language site rules) would remove the guesswork. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

issue.body:
### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking) [https://www.youtube.com/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2F) ### Comment > **Problem: YouTube playlist repeat switches off when AdGuard is enabled.** > > For approximately four months, YouTube's playlist repeat function has stopped working correctly in Google Chrome. > > When I enable repeat, it switches off when the next video starts. This happens across multiple playlists and on three different computers. > > I have updated AdGuard's filters, refreshed YouTube, and tested with another ad-blocking extension disabled. The problem persists. > > **Important test results:** > - With AdGuard enabled, the repeat function switches off between songs. > - With AdGuard disabled, repeat stays enabled across several songs, but YouTube advertisements appear. > - Screenshots showing both situations are attached. > > I have used AdGuard successfully for a long time, and YouTube's repeat function previously worked correctly. > > Please investigate whether an AdGuard filtering rule is interfering with YouTube's playlist repeat function. I would appreciate a solution that allows me to keep blocking advertisements while using repeat. ### Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — mediaoptions.com shows the reporter's timed "DOMAIN DEALS™ / The #⁠1 Domain Name Sales Newsletter" popup as a full-viewport fixed overlay (div#⁠popup.container-popup.popup) that appears once the site's delayed theme scripts run on first interaction. A domain-scoped element-hiding rule was validated end-to-end (visible before, hidden after, page intact, no residue), and the matching shared #⁠#⁠#⁠popup rule in the Popups filter should be extended with this domain. ## Rule `mediaoptions.com###popup` ## Policy rationale The reported element is a newsletter/promotions subscription popup, which the AdGuard Popups filter is documented to block ('Popups and forms for subscribing to news, promotions, and various events'), so no policy rule closes the report. It is not the site's own advertising creative, not a paywall, and not an anti-adblock wall:⁠ the page beneath is fully rendered and scrollable, and the popup only asks users to sign up for a newsletter. Nothing in the run instruction blocks this fix; the maintainer rule on popups supports hiding the popup when the page then works, which the bound vision review confirmed (page integrity intact, no residue, symptom resolved). ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/popups_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/4f2d3a4f89297d3e0736fda5147e5ad00cf354ce/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/popups_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 6537](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/4f2d3a4f89297d3e0736fda5147e5ad00cf354ce/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/popups_specific.txt#L6537). ## Screenshots

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — opentweet.io shows a first-party "We value your privacy" cookie consent banner fixed across the bottom of the page, served by the site's own bundle with no separate CMP vendor request. A domain-scoped element hiding rule for that banner — opentweet.io#⁠#⁠body ⁠> div.fixed.bottom-0:⁠has(a[⁠href="/privacy"]⁠) — was verified against the AdGuard CLI baseline:⁠ the banner is gone after the rule, page integrity intact, no remaining instances. ## Rule `opentweet.io##body > div.fixed.bottom-0:has(a[href="/privacy"])` ## Policy rationale The report is an ordinary cookie-notice annoyance; it is not first-party advertising, a paywall, or an anti-adblock wall, so none of the run instruction's no-rule / policy-close categories applies. Filter policy for the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter:⁠ hiding the notice or blocking the corresponding scripts is sufficient in most cases; the banner here is a fixed overlay that gates no functionality, so hiding it is within policy. No German anti-adblock wall and no anti-adblock detector is involved:⁠ the page is in English and shows no ad-blocker message. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/4f2d3a4f89297d3e0736fda5147e5ad00cf354ce/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

The arrowed "AD/PR" Daiichi Life banner on babytech.jp is a directly sold, site-hosted placement:⁠ its image is served from babytech.jp/wp-content/uploads and it links to the advertiser's own page with rel="sponsored", with no ad-network request anywhere in the captured traffic. Repository policy excludes the site's own first-party advertising from rule generation, so no filter rule is proposed and the report is recommended for closing.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction, Filter policy:⁠ "The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing." The reporter's arrowed element is a directly sold placement whose creative is hosted by the site itself (babytech.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/260224_daiichineo_340x280_03.jpg) inside the site's own "AD/PR" container and links straight to the advertiser's landing page with rel="sponsored" (lp.neofirst.co.jp/daiichi/..., utm_source=babytech&⁠utm_medium=display). Run instruction:⁠ "The agent never closes an issue. 'Recommend closing' below means the report says no rule is needed; a maintainer checks it and decides." No filter-list rule is proposed; the decision is handed to a maintainer. No other policy branch applies:⁠ the page shows no anti-adblock wall, no paywall and no malvertising; no first-party path or vendor host needs a network rule.

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reported interstitial on redhousespice.com is the site's Ad-Shield/Raptive ad-block-recovery wall (gated by the `__adblocker` cookie and navigated to from html-load.com), which the Base filter's Ad-Shield section already blocks per publisher. Full-page vision of the current prepared extension shows the wall absent there because that engine redirects the detector script to noopjs, and apply_rule could not judge the candidate at all (unfiltered phase HTTP 403), so `||html-load.com^$script,domain=redhousespice.com` goes to a maintainer unverified.

## Candidate for review

`||html-load.com^$script,domain=redhousespice.com`

BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt

Not verified: apply_rule stayed inconclusive (validationSkipped, phases [⁠"A"]⁠ only):⁠ "Phase A navigation failed (http_blocked):⁠ main document returned HTTP 403" on both calls, the second refusing a retry, so the candidate was never judged. Complete full-page vision of the current prepared extension session (6/6 tiles inspected, capture 0e4110fb) reports reporterSymptomPresence=absent:⁠ the Ad-Shield wall the reporter screenshotted does not render on this baseline, because the engine serves the detector script from `||ads.adthrive.com/abd/abd.js$xmlhttprequest,redirect=noopjs`, so no `__adblocker` cookie is written and https:⁠//html-load.com/bundle.js is never requested — no phase could show the wall or its removal.

## Missing information

- No guidance for validating reports from Safari content-blocker products (AdGuard Mini for Mac) in the Chromium-extension environment: The run instruction offers two observation routes (Chromium AdGuard browser extension, AdGuard CLI proxy) and declares no route or validation rule for a report from AdGuard Mini for Mac, whose filtering is compiled into Safari content blockers. The reported symptom here depends on the site's ad-block detector XHR to https:⁠//ads.adthrive.com/abd/abd.js:⁠ the Base filter neutralizes it with `$redirect=noopjs`, which the Chromium engine executes (the extension served noopjs, no `__adblocker` cookie was written and the Ad-Shield wall never appeared), so the reported breakage cannot be produced or its fix verified in either advertised blocker. The documents also give no guidance on how to report/validate a candidate whose effect is only observable under a product-specific execution model, which is why this run ends analysis-only with an unverified candidate.

The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

The reported item is a sponsored recommendation carrying Google's own "Реклама" label inside the Google app's Discover feed, i.e. Google's own advertising on Google's own product surface, which the run instruction's filter policy says must not be blocked ("The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing"). Live evidence in the locked AdGuard CLI proxy baseline also shows the reported URL serves the plain Google homepage with no feed, no ad slot and no blank gap, so no rule is proposed.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction:⁠ "The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing." The reported element is a sponsored recommendation served by Google inside Google's own Discover feed, so this branch applies. Run instruction / AdGuard filter policy:⁠ "The site's own advertising should not be deliberately blocked." Blocking Google's own sponsored feed inventory on Google's own property is exactly the deliberate blocking the policy prohibits. No other policy branch applies:⁠ there is no paywall, no German anti-adblock wall, no other anti-adblock wall or detector script (the reachable page shows no gate), and the report is not a scam/phishing/malware case.

issue.title: Remove AI filters from the Other Annoyances
issue.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I checked the documentation and found no answer;
- [x] I checked to make sure that this issue has not already been filed;
- [x] This is not an ad/bug report.

### Problem description

AdGuard Other Annoyances filter blocks AI features such as Google Search Overview.

### Proposed solution

Since AdGuard already offers an AI-annoyance blocking filter list (Stevo's AI Blocklist) I think that rules blocking AI should be removed from the Other Annoyances filter list. Additionally, while the filter provides many useful rules that block unnecessary clutter and other features, some users use these AI features and don't want them blocked, but still want the blocking power of the rest of the filter list. All in all, I think this should be done because there is already a specialized list for this specific purpose that is more comprehensive, and some users want to enable Other Annoyances without blocking AI features.

### Additional information

_No response_

comment.body:
@braverug Yes, Fanboy/Easylist has it's own [dedicated AI annoyance list](https://github.com/easylist/easylist/blob/master/fanboy-addon/fanboy_ai_suggestions.txt).

It's worth noting my list might filter more than the average user would expect from an annoyance list, including things like AI tagged images on social media and image hosting sites, subtle uses of AI functionality some may not find annoying, etc.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The streamcash.to embed page shows an "Ad Blocker Detected / Please disable your ad blocker… to watch" wall over the whole player; it is an element injected into body (random attribute name per load, content in a closed shadow root) that the existing streamcash.to anti-adblock rules do not cover. Adding the domain-scoped element-hiding rule streamcash.to#⁠#⁠body:⁠has(#⁠player-wrap) ⁠> div:⁠not([⁠id]⁠):⁠not([⁠class]⁠) removes the wall and exposes the video.js player — verified in the locked AdGuard CLI baseline (wall visible before, hidden after, page integrity intact). ## Rule `streamcash.to##body:has(#player-wrap) > div:not([id]):not([class])` ## Policy rationale The run instruction blocks report closure only for first-party ads, paywalls, German-language anti-adblock walls and non-anti-adblock scams; this is none of them. The filter policy blocks anti-adblock walls that aggressively insist on disabling the blocker or effectively prevent using the site:⁠ the wall replaces the whole player and demands disabling the ad blocker to watch. The run instruction's gate for other anti-adblock walls is met:⁠ the captured requests show the embed's protection/ad script (https:⁠//streamcash.to/s/0b6b7ba345a6ac.js, keyed by the page payload's 'dk' field, alongside /js/restore.js and /js/embed-player.js) in artifact:⁠har:⁠2909198e-b2ef-4ba8-a259-e920fede7a79. ## Place in the list [BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/23ee3a2c8629d58257ad48c3f93914b6f1bcb425/BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt) Next to the site's existing rules, before [line 2045](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/23ee3a2c8629d58257ad48c3f93914b6f1bcb425/BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt#L2045). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/44951726499 Automated analysis against filters at `23ee3a2`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

Fallback — The page refused to load in the run browser:⁠ main document returned HTTP 403

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The report claims PII is sent to https:⁠//global.ketchcdn.com/web/v3/consent/live_nation/update from ticketmaster.com, and the adguard_cli-style repository inventory shows only ketchcdn /web/v*/log telemetry rules, not this consent-update path. I could not observe it:⁠ the reported URL returned HTTP 403 for the main document on all three allowed browser profile attempts, so no rule was verified and the candidate is handed to a maintainer.

## Candidate for review

`||global.ketchcdn.com/web/v*/consent/live_nation/update$domain=ticketmaster.com`

SpywareFilter/sections/specific.txt

Not verified: Browser access to the reported URL was never available:⁠ the main document returned HTTP 403 on all three allowed profile attempts (desktop en-US, mobile, desktop en-GB with consent accepted), after which the host reported the technical attempt budget exhausted. No HAR, DOM or applied-rules evidence exists for ticketmaster.com, so the reported request to global.ketchcdn.com/web/v3/consent/live_nation/update could not be captured or attributed, and apply_rule could not be run because the page never loaded. The cause of the HTTP 403 is unknown; it is not attributed to bot protection or geo-blocking. The rule is derived from the repository's existing ketchcdn path-pattern family, and its collateral risk (blocking a consent-state write on the site) is untested.

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3
